synthesis.title: How both sides interact
synthesis.contentMarkdown:
**The architectural math for this household:**

Federal-state anti-poverty architecture delivers: **$6,780**
($6,164 federal EITC + $616 state WPTC, both automatic via tax filing)

Philadelphia wage tax extracts: **$1,047**
($420 recoverable via Schedule SP if navigated; $627 stays unrecovered in 95% of cases)

Net experience for this household: **$5,733** (typical case, Schedule SP not claimed)

The federal-state architecture is doing what its design intends; the local extraction is doing what its design intends; the architectural failure is that the two don't reconcile. Both findings are true at once.

designView.title: How to claim what's owed to this household
designView.contentMarkdown:
**Concrete steps:**

1. **File a federal tax return** — even if income is below the filing threshold, federal EITC requires filing. Free options: IRS Free File (income under $79,000), VITA in-person assistance.
2. **Find a VITA site near Strawberry Mansion** — VITA preparers are trained to claim EITC and don't charge fees. Nearest sites are typically open January through April. [Find a site →](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/find-a-location-for-free-tax-help)
3. **Confirm WPTC is claimed automatically** — when the federal return is filed, the PA-40 state return picks up WPTC eligibility. No separate application.
4. **Apply for Schedule SP wage-tax refund** — separate from the federal and state filing. Requires PA Department of Revenue Schedule SP determination of low-income eligibility. [Phila wage tax refund info →](https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/income-taxes/earnings-tax-employees/income-based-wage-tax-refund-petition/)

gapView.title: Where this gap could close
gapView.contentMarkdown:
**Reform pathways currently in development:**

**Schedule SP automation (Philadelphia, City Council):** Cross-agency automation of Schedule SP eligibility — pulling the SP determination from PA filing data rather than requiring a separate state approval — is within the City Council's existing legal authority under the Local Tax Enabling Act. Councilmembers Brooks and O'Rourke have proposed this as part of the People's Tax Plan. [Read the proposal →](TBD)

**VITA expansion (federal-state-local):** The administrative-access failure here is partly a VITA capacity gap. Expanded VITA funding, language access, and outreach would close measurable fractions of the $627-per-household unrecovered amount. Federal VITA appropriations are currently a federal matter; state and city co-investment is within Pennsylvania and Philadelphia's existing authority.

**Federal-state-local credit integration:** A statutory mechanism reconciling federal EITC, state WPTC, and Philadelphia wage tax at the household level would close the architectural gap. No such proposal is currently in development; this is structural reform territory.
